headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Flowise’s writable, networked orchestration can expose shared chatflow inputs/outputs while the prompt-listing agent has no isolation or runtime protections.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is non-runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read/write files and run browser-based flows, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or file handoff, which is unusual and low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated content into A-facing prompt workflows, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to ingest files from a shared directory without sanitization, attacker text can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Disable manual prompt reuse between the two agents.
Store B outputs in a non-shared folder.
Add a short provenance note to any copied text.
Review any file-based ingestion step before execution.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging to B’s flow outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches chatflow inputs/outputs, reads and writes the filesystem, and uses broad network egress, so sensitive content can leave the workspace by default. A is a prompt repository with no runtime data classes, so it is not itself a data source; however, if A is used to seed prompts into B, those contents can be exposed through B’s networked tools.
conditions: IF A-derived prompt text is pasted into B chatflows, B can transmit it to configured model providers or HTTP tools.
IF B is deployed with uploaded files containing secrets, those files can be read and sent onward through networked tools.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in B uploads or chatflow inputs.
Restrict B flows to approved model providers only.
Turn off unnecessary HTTP/search tools in B.
Keep A content in a separate, read-only repository.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before B network calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, but B has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, and broad network egress with shared_state via server datastore. If A content is used to generate or edit B flows, B can overwrite shared files or datastore-backed state without locks. The uncertainty is about the exact deployment, but B’s defaults are already risky.
conditions: IF two B instances operate on the same server datastore, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF A-generated artifacts are imported into B’s writable workspace, B can overwrite them or adjacent files.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per instance.
Disable shared datastore access for concurrent runs.
Make B outputs append-only where possible.
Snapshot the workspace before running paired flows.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared datastore writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt-listing/content-writing source, and B is a graph-based orchestrator that can treat inputs as flow content or tool instructions. That creates a plausible chain where A’s text becomes B’s operational input without verification. Because B can act on networked tools, a mistaken prompt can cascade into incorrect external actions, though not necessarily irreversible ones.
conditions: IF A-generated prompt text is imported into B as a flow node or tool instruction, B may execute it without verification.
IF B is configured to trigger external HTTP/model tools from imported content, errors can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require human review before importing A text into B.
Mark imported content as untrusted in B.
Disable auto-execution on newly imported flows.
Test with a harmless sample flow first.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool nodes run.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source prompt repository with no touched data classes, while B handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets such as model provider keys and tool credentials. The main compliance issue is limited to B’s handling of sensitive operational data; A is not a residency or regulated-data processor here, so the pairwise mismatch is modest.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B chatflows, B’s logging/retention settings become compliance-relevant.
IF A content is repurposed into regulated workflows, the operator must ensure B’s deployment meets the applicable policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B unless approved.
Review B retention and logging settings.
Limit secrets stored in B flows.
Document the data class allowed in each flow.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated inputs.
